import pytest
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient

from app.main import app
from app.settings import load_settings


@pytest.fixture()
def client():
    with TestClient(app) as c:
        yield c


def test_list_items(client):
    r = client.get("/items")
    assert r.status_code == 200
    body = r.json()
    assert body["total"] == 2
    assert [i["sku"] for i in body["items"]] == ["ABC-001", "ABC-002"]
    assert body["items"][1]["name"] == "Red Mug"


def test_filter_by_tag(client):
    r = client.get("/items", params={"tag": "sale"})
    assert [i["sku"] for i in r.json()["items"]] == ["ABC-002"]
    assert client.get("/items", params={"tag": "Sale!"}).status_code == 422


def test_read_item(client):
    assert client.get("/items/ABC-001").json()["name"] == "Blue Mug"
    assert client.get("/items/NOP-000").status_code == 404


def test_create_item(client):
    r = client.post("/items", json={"sku": "XYZ-123", "name": "  fancy   pen ",
                                    "price": 1.25, "tags": ["office"]})
    assert r.status_code == 201
    assert r.json() == {"sku": "XYZ-123", "name": "Fancy Pen", "price": 1.25, "discount": 0.0,
                        "tags": ["office"], "note": None}
    assert client.post("/items", json={"sku": "XYZ-123", "name": "pen", "price": 1,
                                       "tags": ["office"]}).status_code == 409


def test_create_item_rejects_bad_input(client):
    bad = [
        {"sku": "bad", "name": "x", "price": 1, "tags": ["a"]},
        {"sku": "QQQ-001", "name": "x", "price": 1, "tags": []},
        {"sku": "QQQ-002", "name": "x", "price": 1, "discount": 2, "tags": ["a"]},
    ]
    assert [client.post("/items", json=b).status_code for b in bad] == [422, 422, 422]


def test_summary(client):
    assert client.get("/summary").json() == {"count": 2, "value": 14.5, "currency": "EUR"}


def test_settings_from_env(monkeypatch):
    monkeypatch.setenv("INV_CURRENCY", "USD")
    assert load_settings().currency == "USD"
    assert load_settings(page_size=10).page_size == 10

notes: FastAPI 0.95.2 + pydantic 1.10.27 (+ starlette 0.27.0, httpx 0.24.1) on 3.11 -> FastAPI 0.165.0 + pydantic 2.14.4 + pydantic-settings 2.16.3 (+ starlette 1.10.0, httpx 0.28.1) on 3.12: the pydantic v1 -> v2 move people make through FastAPI 0.100. Old side emits NO deprecation warning from the app's calls (pydantic v1 never warns; FastAPI 0.95 has no regex/example/on_event deprecation); the only old-side warning is anyio's BlockingPortal alias from starlette.testclient's import (library internal, not an app call). So expected_warnings holds only the new-side on_event DeprecationWarning, which survives the manual migration (on_event is deliberately left: it still works). Unmigrated on the new side the first failure is the import of app.models (Field regex= raises PydanticUserError at class definition), so every test errors at collection; the per-entry 'breaks' were recorded by leaving one manual edit out at a time (and with direct calls for root_validator). pydantic 1.10.27 is the compiled (Cython) build on 3.11 (G1 territory); pydantic 2 has pydantic-core (Rust). Tests use FastAPI's TestClient (httpx) offline; 422 bodies are only checked by status code because their JSON shape changes in v2 (type 'value_error.missing' -> 'missing', plus 'input'/'url'), which would make the equivalent scenario differ. starlette 1.10 warns 'Using httpx with starlette.testclient is deprecated; install httpx2' at TestClient import (StarletteDeprecationWarning): library internal. manual_migration edits apply to the original text in order; 'if_present' skips a site pymolt already rewrote.
